data.body:
Cross-reference from bug 35f7-a39d-8e27-4922 (sibling sweep of 5546): a hypothesis that
mode 2's non-convergence was caused by a STALE `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` — from the
bare `git fetch origin tickets` at reconcile-bridge.yml:286/309 — has been experimentally
**REFUTED**. Recording it here so the dead hypothesis does not get re-raised.

The mechanism is real in general (a bare fetch only opportunistically writes the
remote-tracking ref, and under a narrow configured refspec leaves it stale), but its
precondition does not hold in CI: `actions/checkout` builds the workspace with
`git remote add`, which installs the wildcard `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`.
Verified directly against run **30585738860**, whose log shows the bare fetch advancing
the ref on every retry:

    60ccc6506..4d37b6925  tickets -> origin/tickets
    4d37b6925..dd70be0d7  tickets -> origin/tickets
    dd70be0d7..a46013f4c  tickets -> origin/tickets
    a46013f4c..f3a1fe61f  tickets -> origin/tickets

This independently corroborates this ticket's own Phase 1 finding that "all five merges
SUCCEEDED and integrated five distinct remote SHAs" — the loop was converging and losing
a genuine push race, which is what 4c4f addressed. No change to this ticket's disposition;
35f7 is fixing the same construct in `_store/push.py`, where the narrow-refspec
precondition DOES hold, and hardening the workflow sites as a behavioural no-op.
